Hilaire Belloc, The Four Men.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/hilaire-belloc/the-four-men

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Hilaire Belloc, the author, died 1953.

First publication of the text used: 1911, in the United Kingdom (SE colophon: 'The Four Men was published in 1911 by Hilaire Belloc.'; the Wikipedia infobox for 'The Four Men: A Farrago' lists the country United Kingdom and the publisher T. Nelson & Sons, and no US edition).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1911, before 1931; a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2006.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1953, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2024.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
